note: Reference only. No meme image, clip or sound ships with this repository. Read memes/README.md before using any of these.

fields.format: image, gif, video or sound: the usual form of the meme.
fields.timing_s: Typical on-screen duration [min, max] in seconds. Text on it still follows max(1.5 s, words x 0.33 s + 0.5 s).
fields.rights.kind: stock, tv, film, animation, game, music, webcomic, user-generated, trope (a technique nobody owns) or unknown.
fields.content_id_risk: Chance of an automated YouTube Content ID match if you use the ORIGINAL media in a monetized video: low, medium or high. It is not the legal risk; a low score still allows a manual claim or a takedown.
fields.how_to_recreate: How to make an original version with graphics/ or HyperFrames that keeps the joke and leaves the copyrighted media out.

memes.name: Distracted Boyfriend
memes.what_it_means: Someone abandons what they have for something new and shiny. Three labels: the person, the old thing, the new thing.
memes.when_to_use: A team tempted by the new framework while the old one still works; a user ignoring the feature you just built.
memes.how_to_recreate: Three labeled cards or icons: one in the middle ("you") with an arrow-curved from graphics/ pointing away from the left card ("the tool that works") toward the right card ("new shiny tool"). Keep the three labels; drop the photo.
memes.origin: Stock photo by Barcelona photographer Antonio Guillem, shot in 2015 and sold on iStock and Shutterstock; it went viral as a meme in 2017.

rights.likely_owner: Antonio Guillem (photographer), licensed through stock agencies.

content_id_risk.reason: Content ID matches video and audio, so a still shown for a few seconds is unlikely to be matched automatically; the owner can still file a manual claim or takedown. It is a licensable stock photo, so using it unlicensed is a plain license breach.

sourcing.label: License
sourcing.url: Search Antonio Guillem's portfolio on iStock or Shutterstock and buy a standard license for the frame

tone_warnings: Built on a man ogling a woman; reads as sexist to part of the audience.
Very familiar since 2017; can feel dated.

content_id_risk.reason: A clip from a creator's video; claims are possible and the creator is a professional with brand deals.

tone_warnings: Real person's likeness; dated (2019).

memes.name: Trade Offer
memes.what_it_means: "I receive X, you receive Y": a lopsided deal.
memes.when_to_use: Explaining a trade-off: "I receive: 2 minutes of setup. You receive: no more manual imports."
memes.how_to_recreate: Two-column card ("I receive" / "You receive") with items entering as the voice says them. Keep the joke; drop the person and the audio.
memes.origin: TikTok format from 2021 (see KYM for the creators); the popular version has a short music sting.

rights.likely_owner: The TikTok creators; the audio's owner: unknown.

content_id_risk.reason: Reusing the original clip brings its music sting along, and music is what Content ID matches most.

memes.name: Record scratch freeze frame ("Yep, that's me")
memes.what_it_means: Freeze on a chaotic moment while a narrator says "Yep, that's me. You're probably wondering how I got here."
memes.when_to_use: Cold open: show the broken end state first, freeze, then rewind to explain. Fits the "result first" hook rule.
memes.how_to_recreate: Freeze the frame (PNG freeze per the skill's freeze recipe), slight desaturation on the wrapper, a short scratch sound you generate or take CC0, and your own voice line. The format is a cliche nobody owns.
memes.origin: Film and TV cliche of a freeze frame with narration; KYM documents the "Yep, that's me" meme format from 2015-2016.

rights.likely_owner: Nobody owns the technique; any clip or song you reuse has its own owner.

content_id_risk.reason: Your own freeze, voice and sound: nothing to match. High if you lift a film clip or a song for it.

tone_warnings: Overused as an opener; keep it short.

memes.name: Dramatic zoom (Dramatic Chipmunk)
memes.what_it_means: A sudden dramatic punch-in on a face or detail with a dramatic music sting.
memes.when_to_use: Mock-dramatic reveal of a tiny detail ("and then... the semicolon").
memes.how_to_recreate: Punch-in on the wrapper from 1.0 to the skill's 1.10 limit in about 0.3 s (a deliberate exception to the slow zoom; keep it rare), a dark vignette, and an original three-note sting.
memes.origin: Clip of a prairie dog (not a chipmunk) from the Japanese TV show "Hello! Morning", uploaded to YouTube in June 2007 with music from the film Young Frankenstein (1974).

rights.likely_owner: The Japanese broadcaster (footage) and the film's music rights holders.

content_id_risk.reason: TV footage plus a film score: both are the kind of reference Content ID holds.

tone_warnings: Dated (2007); a breakneck zoom can feel cheap in a serious tutorial.

memes.name: To Be Continued (JoJo)
memes.what_it_means: Freeze on a cliffhanger with a "To be continued" arrow and a guitar riff.
memes.when_to_use: Outro of part 1 of a series, or before a fail is shown after a break.
memes.how_to_recreate: Freeze frame with a slight sepia, an arrow-straight with "To be continued" text sliding in from the left, and original music. Never the Yes song.
memes.origin: End card of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure anime (2012), which uses the song "Roundabout" by Yes (1971); popular as a meme on Vine from 2016.

rights.likely_owner: The song's publishers and label (Yes, "Roundabout"); David Production / Shueisha for the anime card.

content_id_risk.reason: "Roundabout" is a commercial recording; using it in a monetized video is a likely Content ID match.

tone_warnings: Dated (2016).

memes.name: Curb Your Enthusiasm outro ("Directed by Robert B. Weide")
memes.what_it_means: Freeze on an awkward failure, cut to credits and a jaunty tuba tune.
memes.when_to_use: End a blooper or a failed attempt shown on purpose.
memes.how_to_recreate: Freeze, cut to a black card with your own credits text, and an original jaunty tune. The credit with a real director's name is not yours to use.
memes.origin: HBO's Curb Your Enthusiasm end credits and the theme "Frolic" by Luciano Michelini (originally from a 1974 Italian film).

rights.likely_owner: HBO / the show's producers (the credits) and the composition's publisher ("Frolic").

content_id_risk.reason: "Frolic" is a commercial composition; it is a likely Content ID match.

tone_warnings: Uses a real person's name (the director) in the credit; dated.

memes.name: SpongeBob time card ("A few moments later")
memes.what_it_means: A narrator-voiced card that skips time.
memes.when_to_use: Skipping a wait: an install, a render, an import. Matches the skill's rule of cutting waits.
memes.how_to_recreate: chapter-card or a smaller text card with "A few moments later" in a playful font you license (OFL), read by your own voice. Not the show's cards or voice.
memes.origin: Title cards from SpongeBob SquarePants (from 1999), read by a French-accented narrator; reaction images from around 2009.

rights.likely_owner: Nickelodeon (Paramount).

content_id_risk.reason: The card images and narration come from the show's video and audio, which is matchable.

memes.name: Hackerman / "I'm in"
memes.what_it_means: Over-the-top movie hacker typing fast and declaring "I'm in".
memes.when_to_use: Self-irony when doing something mundane in a terminal (running a script, changing a setting).
memes.how_to_recreate: Your own terminal recording sped up, green-on-black text, and "I'm in." in a tooltip. The "I'm in" line is a movie cliche nobody owns.
memes.origin: Character Hackerman from the short film Kung Fury (2015, David Sandberg); the "I'm in" line is an older hacker-movie cliche.

rights.likely_owner: Laser Unicorns / David Sandberg (Kung Fury).

content_id_risk.reason: Kung Fury was released free online but is still copyrighted; footage reuse can be claimed.

tone_warnings: Typing sped up past 1.5x breaks the skill's speed rule; keep the joke in the text.

memes.name: Coffin Dance
memes.what_it_means: A failure so bad it gets a funeral.
memes.when_to_use: Almost never in a tutorial. Avoid in anything about real loss.
memes.how_to_recreate: Not recreatable without the footage and the song; use a cross plus a short sad-trombone of your own instead.
memes.origin: Ghanaian pallbearers (Nana Otafrija Pallbearing Service) dancing with a coffin, set to "Astronomia" by Tony Igy (Vicetone remix); peak meme in March 2020.

rights.likely_owner: The footage's owner: unknown; "Astronomia": Tony Igy and the remix's label.

content_id_risk.reason: "Astronomia" is a commercial recording; very likely matched.

tone_warnings: About death and real funerals; peaked during the 2020 pandemic, so it can read as insensitive.

memes.name: Rickroll
memes.what_it_means: Bait-and-switch: you expected something and got "Never Gonna Give You Up".
memes.when_to_use: Avoid in tutorials: baiting viewers wastes their time. At most mention it in an explainer about internet culture.
memes.how_to_recreate: Don't recreate the song. A text-only nod ("no, it's not a rickroll") is enough.
memes.origin: Rick Astley's single "Never Gonna Give You Up" (1987, RCA); the bait-link prank spread around 2007.

rights.likely_owner: The recording's label (RCA, now Sony Music) and the song's publishers.

content_id_risk.reason: Major-label recording and music video: one of the most likely Content ID matches there is.

tone_warnings: Dated; misleads the viewer.

memes.name: Deal With It (sunglasses drop)
memes.what_it_means: Pixel sunglasses drop onto a face: smug confidence.
memes.when_to_use: After a clean, confident solution: "one line. Deal with it."
memes.how_to_recreate: Draw your own pixel sunglasses as an SVG (simple rectangles) and drop them in with a GSAP y tween, plus a short CC0 click. The look is generic.
memes.origin: Animated pixel sunglasses format standardized around 2010 (KYM credits a dump.fm contest); the phrase is older.

rights.likely_owner: Nobody clearly owns the format; specific GIFs: unknown.

content_id_risk.reason: Your own drawing; nothing to match.

memes.name: Nyan Cat
memes.what_it_means: Absurd, endless, joyful loop.
memes.when_to_use: Almost never in a tutorial; maybe as an ironic "loading" gag.
memes.how_to_recreate: An original looping progress-bar with a rainbow gradient fill; no cat, no song.
memes.origin: Animation by Chris Torres (April 2011) set to the song "Nyanyanyanyanyanyanya!" by daniwell (2010); Torres sold the original as an NFT in 2021.

rights.likely_owner: Chris Torres (animation); daniwell (song).

content_id_risk.reason: The song has an identifiable owner and the animation is actively managed by its creator.

tone_warnings: Dated (2011).

memes.name: Wasted (GTA)
memes.what_it_means: Slow-motion, desaturated fail with a big "WASTED" title.
memes.when_to_use: A dramatic fail shown on purpose (the app crashes), as a joke.
memes.how_to_recreate: Desaturate and slow the wrapper (only on your own footage, not a tutorial step), and a generic serif title like "FAILED" in your own type. No game font or sound.
memes.origin: Death screen of the Grand Theft Auto games (Rockstar Games); the GTA V version is the meme.

rights.likely_owner: Rockstar Games / Take-Two Interactive.

content_id_risk.reason: Game footage and its sound are matchable; Take-Two is known to enforce.

tone_warnings: Built on character death in a violent game; slow-motion breaks the tutorial speed rule.

memes.name: Mission Failed, We'll Get 'Em Next Time
memes.what_it_means: A fail treated like a lost video-game mission.
memes.when_to_use: Light-hearted fail before showing the fix.
memes.how_to_recreate: Your own voice reading a similar line over a cross from graphics/status, with a low CC0 impact.
memes.origin: Voice line from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 (Infinity Ward / Activision, 2009); a Vine fail meme from 2016.

rights.likely_owner: Activision (game audio) and the voice actor's performance.

content_id_risk.reason: Game audio owned by a large publisher; enforcement on memes is not documented but it is claimable.

tone_warnings: Military-shooter framing; dated.

memes.name: Windows XP error (sound and dialog)
memes.what_it_means: A system error noise: something went wrong.
memes.when_to_use: A real error in the demo, or a list of things that go wrong.
memes.how_to_recreate: A short CC0 error sound from library/ and a generic dialog card of your own. No Windows chrome, icons or sounds.
memes.origin: System sounds and dialogs of Microsoft Windows XP (2001); remixes became a meme.

rights.likely_owner: Microsoft (sounds and UI design).

content_id_risk.reason: Microsoft owns the sounds; matches of short system sounds are uncommon but claimable, and the UI chrome is trade dress.

tone_warnings: Copying the OS look can imply Microsoft endorsement.

memes.name: Sad trombone (wah wah wah)
memes.what_it_means: A descending "wah wah wah wahhh": a letdown.
memes.when_to_use: A failed attempt or a disappointing result shown on purpose.
memes.how_to_recreate: Record or synthesize four descending notes yourself, or take a CC0 version and log it in library/LICENSES.md.
memes.origin: A brass gag from early 20th-century vaudeville and cartoons; a web meme around 2008-2010.

rights.likely_owner: Nobody owns the gag; every specific recording has its own owner.

content_id_risk.reason: Low with your own or a CC0 recording; a recording lifted from a library or a show can match.

tone_warnings: Overused; one per video.

memes.name: Crickets (awkward silence)
memes.what_it_means: Nobody laughs or responds.
memes.when_to_use: After a joke that falls flat, or a feature nobody uses.
memes.how_to_recreate: A CC0 field recording of crickets at low level, under a held frame. Watch the skill's silence rule (3 s warning, 6 s cap without voice).
memes.origin: Comedy cliche from radio and TV; no single origin.

rights.likely_owner: Nobody owns the gag; every recording has its own owner.

content_id_risk.reason: Low with a CC0 or own recording.

sourcing.label: Sound source
sourcing.url: Search CC0 field recordings (e.g. freesound.org filtered by CC0) and log the license

memes.name: Rimshot (ba dum tss)
memes.what_it_means: Drum sting after a pun or a bad joke.
memes.when_to_use: Right after a deliberate pun in the voice.
memes.how_to_recreate: A CC0 drum sting or one you record; no visual needed, or a quick punch-in.
memes.origin: Drum fill from vaudeville and stand-up comedy; no single origin.

rights.likely_owner: Nobody owns the gag; every recording has its own owner.

content_id_risk.reason: Low with a CC0 or own recording.

tone_warnings: Cheesy on purpose; one per video.

memes.name: Vine boom
memes.what_it_means: A deep, sudden boom that punctuates a reveal or a stare.
memes.when_to_use: Reveal of a surprising number, sparingly.
memes.how_to_recreate: A CC0 impact from library/ (pick the deepest), 2-4 frames before the reveal, per the skill's SFX rules.
memes.origin: KYM traces it to a metallic impact in a 2012 Bluezone Corporation sample pack; popular on Vine from 2014.

rights.likely_owner: Bluezone Corporation (per KYM); the pack's license terms: check them before use.

content_id_risk.reason: Third parties re-upload and sometimes register popular meme sounds; the original is a commercial sample.

tone_warnings: Overused and loud; at most once per video, never on every cut.

memes.name: Bruh sound
memes.what_it_means: Deadpan "bruh": disbelief at something dumb.
memes.when_to_use: Reacting to a silly bug, as a voice line.
memes.how_to_recreate: Your own voice line, recorded or TTS with your brand voice.
memes.origin: Vine from 2014 (per KYM, a dubbed voice-over on a basketball clip).

rights.likely_owner: The voice-over's creator (per KYM); unknown otherwise.

content_id_risk.reason: A recording with an owner; re-uploads may be registered by third parties.

tone_warnings: Slangy; can feel disrespectful toward the viewer.

memes.name: Roblox "oof"
memes.what_it_means: A short grunt for a small fail.
memes.when_to_use: A minor mistake in a light-hearted explainer.
memes.how_to_recreate: Your own short voice grunt.
memes.origin: Death sound used by Roblox, taken from the game Messiah (2000); after a licensing dispute with composer Tommy Tallarico, Roblox removed it in July 2022.

rights.likely_owner: Disputed: claimed by Tommy Tallarico; Roblox licensed it for a time.

content_id_risk.reason: Ownership was disputed and enforced against Roblox itself; avoid the original.

tone_warnings: Its ownership dispute is public; don't use it.

memes.name: Jeopardy "Think!" (waiting music)
memes.what_it_means: Waiting-music jingle while someone thinks.
memes.when_to_use: Avoid: cut waits instead (skill rule). At most a short "think about it" pause in an explainer.
memes.how_to_recreate: An original 4-6 s waiting loop at low level, or simply cut the wait.
memes.origin: "Think!" composed by Merv Griffin for the game show Jeopardy! (1960s).

rights.likely_owner: Merv Griffin's estate; the publisher: unknown.

content_id_risk.reason: A well-known commercial composition; likely to be matched.

memes.name: Inception "BRAAAM"
memes.what_it_means: A huge brass blast: epic, ominous moment.
memes.when_to_use: Ironic epic reveal of something tiny.
memes.how_to_recreate: Layer a low synth pad and a brass-like CC0 sample, or generate a short original sting.
memes.origin: Brass blast from the film Inception (2010) and its trailers; authorship is disputed (Hans Zimmer and trailer composers).

rights.likely_owner: Warner Bros. and the composers; authorship disputed.

content_id_risk.reason: Film score and trailer music are typical Content ID references.

tone_warnings: Cliche; loud.

memes.name: Metal Gear alert ("!")
memes.what_it_means: A sharp alert sting with a red exclamation mark: "you've been spotted".
memes.when_to_use: When the viewer should notice a warning or an error that pops up.
memes.how_to_recreate: A red "!" drawn by you above the element (tooltip with a single glyph) and a short CC0 notification sound.
memes.origin: Enemy alert sound and "!" icon from Metal Gear Solid (Konami, 1998).

rights.likely_owner: Konami.

content_id_risk.reason: Game audio owned by Konami; claimable.

memes.name: "Oh no, oh no, oh no no no no no"
memes.what_it_means: Something is about to go very wrong.
memes.when_to_use: Right before a fail you show on purpose.
memes.how_to_recreate: Your own voice saying "oh no" over a held frame, or an original short sting. Never the song.
memes.origin: Song "Oh No" by Capone, which samples The Shangri-Las' "Remember (Walking in the Sand)" (1964); viral on TikTok. Release year of Capone's track: unknown (sources disagree).

rights.likely_owner: Capone's label and publishers, plus the sample's rights holders.

content_id_risk.reason: A commercial recording with a cleared or uncleared sample; likely to be matched.
